en: How do you process thousands of raw instrument files without ingesting chaos? Explore the automated pipeline that fingerprints, validates, and routes measurements in real time.
es: ¿Cómo se procesan miles de ficheros de instrumento en crudo sin ingerir caos? Recorre el pipeline automatizado que toma huella, valida y enruta las medidas en tiempo real.

en: Thousands of instrument files across nine formats, none linked to its synthesis. Processing **6,073 raw files** by hand would mean endless manual retyping and inevitable human error.

en: Instead, the workflow takes over. Incoming files are authenticated, fingerprinted against duplicates, and routed by technique: deterministic parsers handle tabular data, while specialized AI agents extract unstructured PDF reports and microscopy images, **logging every step to an audit trail**.
es: En su lugar, se encarga el workflow. Los ficheros que entran se autentican, se les toma huella contra duplicados y se enrutan por técnica: los parsers deterministas se ocupan de los datos tabulares, mientras agentes de IA especializados extraen informes PDF sin estructura e imágenes de microscopía, **registrando cada paso en una traza de auditoría**.

en: The RAG assistant **never writes SQL**. Every one of its tools is a call to a stored function with typed parameters, so what it can ask is fixed by the schema rather than by how carefully a prompt was worded. `agent_verify_owner()` decides whether the answer carries exact values or coarse ones: it receives a token, hands on a **boolean**, and stores neither.
es: El asistente RAG **nunca escribe SQL**. Cada una de sus herramientas es una llamada a una función almacenada con parámetros tipados, así que lo que puede preguntar lo fija el esquema y no lo cuidadosa que fuera la redacción de un prompt. `agent_verify_owner()` decide si la respuesta lleva valores exactos o aproximados: recibe un token, pasa un **booleano** y no guarda ninguno de los dos.

en: What those functions can read
es: Qué pueden leer esas funciones

en: Five years of chemistry lived in one spreadsheet, a folder of instrument files, and a stack of handwritten notebooks. This is what it became: a single governed schema where every column has a documented meaning and every automated action leaves a trace.
es: Cinco años de química vivían en una hoja de cálculo, una carpeta de ficheros de instrumento y una pila de cuadernos manuscritos. Esto es en lo que se convirtió: un único esquema gobernado donde cada columna tiene un significado documentado y cada acción automática deja rastro.

en: The views everything reads through
es: Las vistas por las que se lee todo

en: Nothing queries a raw table if a view exists for it. A view decides a join once, instead of having it re-invented in every script, and it can be documented, versioned and pointed at.
es: Nada consulta una tabla en crudo si existe una vista para ella. Una vista decide un JOIN una sola vez, en lugar de reinventarlo en cada script, y se puede documentar, versionar y señalar.

en: Why a database, and not a very good spreadsheet
es: Por qué una base de datos, y no una hoja de cálculo muy buena

en: A header reading `T` could be temperature, time or a code. **Every column carries a native `COMMENT`** with its units and allowed values, and pgAdmin, this site and the AI agent read the same one.
es: Una cabecera que pone `T` puede ser temperatura, tiempo o un código. **Cada columna lleva un `COMMENT` nativo** con sus unidades y sus valores permitidos, y pgAdmin, esta web y el agente de IA leen el mismo.

en: A measurement cannot exist without its synthesis (foreign key). A model cannot be registered as irreproducible without a written reason (`CHECK`). **The database enforces this**, not the scripts that write to it.
es: Una medida no puede existir sin su síntesis (clave foránea). Un modelo no se puede registrar como irreproducible sin un motivo escrito (`CHECK`). **Lo impone la base de datos**, no los scripts que escriben en ella.

en: A notebook ingests the master Excel file; a workflow ingests instrument files. The notebook loads by `UPSERT` and never `DELETE`, so it **cannot erase what the workflow wrote overnight**.
es: Un cuaderno ingiere el Excel maestro; un workflow ingiere los ficheros de instrumento. El cuaderno carga por `UPSERT` y nunca por `DELETE`, así que **no puede borrar lo que el workflow escribió de madrugada**.

en: Every automated action lands in `audit_log` with a typed verdict and cause; every agent exchange in `agent_chat_log`. Both are **written by code, never by an LLM**, so the system being recorded cannot edit its own record.
es: Cada acción automática aterriza en `audit_log` con veredicto y causa tipados; cada intercambio del agente, en `agent_chat_log`. Los dos se **escriben por código, nunca por un LLM**, así que el sistema registrado no puede editar su propio registro.

en: The schema documents itself in a **table**: `data_dictionary` holds one row per column, so the site and the agent read it instead of carrying a copy. Coverage is checkable, and the target is 100 % because a gap makes **"undocumented column" and "column that does not exist" indistinguishable**.
es: El esquema se documenta a sí mismo en una **tabla**: `data_dictionary` guarda una fila por columna, así que la web y el agente la leen en vez de llevar una copia. La cobertura es comprobable, y el objetivo es el 100 % porque un hueco hace **indistinguibles "columna sin documentar" y "columna que no existe"**.

en: Play with the synthesis conditions and watch the prediction move — then see what keeps this from being a loose pickle file on somebody’s laptop.
es: Juega con las condiciones de síntesis y mira cómo se mueve la predicción; luego mira qué impide que esto sea un fichero pickle suelto en el portátil de alguien.

en: A compass, not an oracle
es: Una brújula, no un oráculo

en: Think of the synthesis space as a map in the dark. The experiments already run light up a few patches of it. A predictive model is not a machine that tells you the answer — it is **a compass**: it points at the direction where walking would light up the most new ground.
es: Piensa en el espacio de síntesis como un mapa a oscuras. Los experimentos ya hechos iluminan unos pocos trozos. Un modelo predictivo no es una máquina que da la respuesta: es **una brújula**, y apunta hacia donde caminar iluminaría más terreno nuevo.

en: And the direction it points is not "where crystals are most likely". An experiment run where the model is already confident confirms what it knew. The useful place is **where it hesitates**, because either outcome there corrects it. That is what the map below measures: the entropy of the predicted distribution, cell by cell.
es: Y la dirección que señala no es "donde hay más probabilidad de cristales". Un experimento hecho donde el modelo ya está seguro confirma lo que ya sabía. El sitio útil es **donde duda**, porque allí cualquiera de los dos resultados lo corrige. Eso es lo que mide el mapa de abajo: la entropía de la distribución predicha, casilla a casilla.

en: **Most of the plane has never been visited.** Even for Ca, the metal with the most history behind it, the syntheses pile up in a handful of cells.
es: **La mayor parte del plano no se ha visitado nunca.** Incluso para el Ca, el metal con más historia detrás, las síntesis se amontonan en un puñado de casillas.

en: **The model hesitates almost everywhere**, including where the laboratory has looked.
es: **El modelo duda casi en todas partes**, incluso donde el laboratorio sí ha mirado.

en: **Because conditions were swept while the chemistry changed alongside them**, so the record cannot separate the two.
es: **Porque las condiciones se barrieron mientras la química cambiaba a la vez**, así que el registro no puede separar las dos cosas.

en: The map and the model diagnostics point at the same experiment from opposite ends: the next plate worth running is **one that varies conditions finely while holding the metal and linker fixed**.
es: El mapa y el diagnóstico del modelo señalan el mismo experimento desde extremos opuestos: la siguiente placa que merece la pena es **una que varíe las condiciones con finura manteniendo fijos el metal y el conector**.

en: A model is not a file
es: Un modelo no es un fichero

en: The usual way to keep a trained model is a `.pkl` in a folder, and it fails in a specific way: six months later the file is still there and **nothing around it is**. Which rows trained it, which columns, which version of the code, what it actually scored.
es: La forma habitual de guardar un modelo entrenado es un `.pkl` en una carpeta, y falla de una manera concreta: seis meses después el fichero sigue ahí y **no sigue nada de lo que había alrededor**. Qué filas lo entrenaron, qué columnas, qué versión del código, qué puntuó de verdad.

en: So the model lives in the database as **five related tables**, and the binary is the least important of them. The other four hold the recipe, and with a complete recipe the binary can be rebuilt.
es: Así que el modelo vive en la base de datos como **cinco tablas relacionadas**, y el binario es la menos importante. Las otras cuatro guardan la receta, y con una receta completa el binario se puede reconstruir.

en: The literal SQL that selected the rows, plus its SHA-256. Two models sharing a query but differing in row count were **not** trained on the same thing, and the hash makes that difference detectable.
es: El SQL literal que seleccionó las filas, más su SHA-256. Dos modelos que comparten consulta pero difieren en número de filas **no** se entrenaron sobre lo mismo, y el hash hace detectable esa diferencia.

en: Algorithm, hyperparameters, random seed, library versions, and the exact git commit. Also the status — active, superseded, archived or **invalid** — and a `CHECK` that refuses to mark a model irreproducible without writing why.
es: Algoritmo, hiperparámetros, semilla aleatoria, versiones de las librerías y el commit exacto de git. También el estado (activo, superado, archivado o **inválido**) y un `CHECK` que se niega a marcar un modelo como irreproducible sin escribir por qué.

en: Every input column with its position in the contract, and every **excluded** one with the reason it was excluded. `reactor_volume_ml` is recorded as zero-variance, `fill_fraction` as perfectly collinear with it.
es: Cada columna de entrada con su posición en el contrato, y cada una **excluida** con el motivo de la exclusión. `reactor_volume_ml` queda registrada como varianza cero, y `fill_fraction` como perfectamente colineal con ella.

en: Metrics in long format — one row per metric, per class, per split — so adding a new metric never means altering the schema.
es: Métricas en formato largo, una fila por métrica, por clase y por partición, así que añadir una métrica nueva nunca obliga a alterar el esquema.

en: The serialised pipeline with a SHA-256 checked on every load. It sits in its own table so a light backup can skip it: it is the only part that a complete recipe can regenerate.
es: El pipeline serializado con un SHA-256 que se comprueba en cada carga. Vive en su propia tabla para que una copia de seguridad ligera pueda saltárselo: es la única parte que una receta completa puede regenerar.

en: One more thing decides which model the simulator is actually running: a **deployment slot**. The simulator does not name a model; it asks the database which one occupies the `primary` slot. When a model name was written into this file by hand instead, retraining to correct a unit error of a factor of a thousand left **the site serving the superseded model with nothing raising an error**: an obsolete model returns predictions as readily as a current one.
es: Una cosa más decide qué modelo está ejecutando el simulador de verdad: una **ranura de despliegue**. El simulador no nombra un modelo; le pregunta a la base de datos cuál ocupa la ranura `primary`. Cuando en su lugar se escribió a mano el nombre de un modelo en este fichero, reentrenar para corregir un error de unidades de un factor de mil dejó **la web sirviendo el modelo superado sin que nada diera error**: un modelo obsoleto devuelve predicciones con la misma facilidad que uno vigente.

es: Reflexiones emergentes y más anchas: FWHM mediana de 0,240°, incluso más ancha que la amorfa

en: Moderate peak-to-background ratios; descriptors sit midway between halo and crystalline order, making it **the most challenging class for the classifier**
es: Relaciones pico-fondo moderadas; sus descriptores quedan a medio camino entre el halo y el orden cristalino, lo que la convierte en **la clase más difícil para el clasificador**

en: Sharp, intense Bragg reflections
es: Reflexiones de Bragg afiladas e intensas

en: Intense, narrow peaks at low angles — median FWHM 0.162°, well under 0.20°
es: Picos intensos y estrechos a ángulos bajos: FWHM mediana de 0,162°, bastante por debajo de 0,20°

en: Signal-to-noise and peak-to-background jump orders of magnitude over amorphous (0.03 → 9.42)
es: La señal-ruido y la relación pico-fondo suben órdenes de magnitud sobre la amorfa (0,03 → 9,42)

en: Crystalline fraction accounts for the vast majority of scattered intensity; the pipeline trusts 99% of these
es: La fracción cristalina se lleva la inmensa mayoría de la intensidad dispersada; el pipeline se fía del 99 % de estas

en: `scherrer_size_nm` mathematically requires a real Bragg peak, yet it comes out **larger for amorphous samples (37.4 nm) than for incipient ones (33.8 nm)** — physically absurd, since an amorphous solid has no crystallites. Calculated over baseline noise, the formula still returns a number: a reminder that a physical formula only applies within its intended domain.
es: `scherrer_size_nm` exige matemáticamente un pico de Bragg real, y sin embargo sale **mayor para las muestras amorfas (37,4 nm) que para las incipientes (33,8 nm)**: físicamente absurdo, porque un sólido amorfo no tiene cristalitos. Calculada sobre el ruido de la línea base, la fórmula devuelve un número igualmente: un recordatorio de que una fórmula física solo vale dentro del dominio para el que se dedujo.

en: A categorical label like "Fe" hides the physics and collapses **Fe(II)** (92 pm) and **Fe(III)** (78.5 pm) into the same bin. Replacing chemical symbols with **eight fundamental properties** (Shannon ionic radius, electronegativity, HSAB hardness, charge-to-radius ratio) enables the model to interpolate across the periodic table and predict outcomes for unseen metals
es: Una etiqueta categórica como "Fe" esconde la física y mete **Fe(II)** (92 pm) y **Fe(III)** (78,5 pm) en el mismo saco. Sustituir los símbolos químicos por **ocho propiedades fundamentales** (radio iónico de Shannon, electronegatividad, dureza HSAB, relación carga-radio) permite al modelo interpolar por la tabla periódica y predecir resultados para metales que no ha visto

en: Molecule names convey no spatial or chemical meaning. Using RDKit, each linker is featurized into **six geometric and topological descriptors**: denticity (binding points), max donor distance (pore-size proxy), acidic proton count, and rotatable bonds (flexibility)—capturing the structural rules of reticular assembly.
es: Los nombres de molécula no transmiten significado espacial ni químico. Con RDKit, cada conector se convierte en **seis descriptores geométricos y topológicos**: denticidad (puntos de unión), distancia máxima entre donores (aproximación al tamaño de poro), número de protones ácidos y enlaces rotables (flexibilidad), que capturan las reglas estructurales del ensamblaje reticular.

en: A spreadsheet of recipes becomes a governed table
es: Una hoja de recetas se convierte en una tabla gobernada

en: What the chemist controls: metal, linker, solvent, temperature, time, modulator. Structured data that was never structured properly.
es: Lo que controla el químico: metal, conector, disolvente, temperatura, tiempo, modulador. Datos estructurados que nunca se estructuraron bien.

en: Notebooks 02 & 05
es: Cuadernos 02 y 05

en: A diffractogram becomes 29 comparable numbers
es: Un difractograma se convierte en 29 números comparables

en: What the material answers back. Raw instrument curves that have to be processed before any two of them can be compared.
es: Lo que responde el material. Curvas de instrumento en crudo que hay que procesar antes de poder comparar dos cualesquiera.

en: The rigid core the linker is built on. Governs the size of the pore that can form.
es: El núcleo rígido sobre el que se construye el conector. Gobierna el tamaño del poro que puede formarse.

en: How many points the linker can bind through. Two makes a chain, three or more makes a network.
es: Por cuántos puntos puede unirse el conector. Dos dan una cadena; tres o más, una red.

en: How many protons have to leave before the linker can coordinate — which is what ties the outcome to pH and to the modulator.
es: Cuántos protones tienen que salir antes de que el conector pueda coordinar, que es lo que ata el resultado al pH y al modulador.

en: The distance between the outermost binding points, in ångström. The first-order estimate of pore size.
es: La distancia entre los puntos de unión más externos, en ångström. La estimación de primer orden del tamaño de poro.

en: Whether the binding groups arrive masked as esters and have to be freed in situ.
es: Si los grupos de unión llegan enmascarados como ésteres y hay que liberarlos in situ.

en: Conformational freedom. A floppy linker is far less likely to give an ordered framework.
es: Libertad conformacional. Un conector flexible tiene muchas menos probabilidades de dar una red ordenada.

en: How strongly the metal pulls electron density from the linker. The classic scale.
es: Con cuánta fuerza atrae el metal la densidad electrónica del conector. La escala clásica.

en: A second scale, computed from spectroscopic energies. Computed here, but **dropped before training**: it is undefined for the lanthanides, so for Ce, La, Nd and Dy the value does not exist rather than being missing. Screen 04 tells that story.
es: Una segunda escala, calculada a partir de energías espectroscópicas. Se calcula aquí, pero se **descarta antes de entrenar**: no está definida para los lantánidos, así que para Ce, La, Nd y Dy el valor no existe, más que faltar. La pantalla 04 cuenta esa historia.

en: Resistance to deformation of the electron cloud. Hard metals prefer hard donors — the HSAB rule, as a number.
es: Resistencia a la deformación de la nube electrónica. Los metales duros prefieren donores duros: la regla HSAB, convertida en número.

en: Affinity for oxygen donors, which is what a carboxylate linker offers.
es: Afinidad por donores de oxígeno, que es lo que ofrece un conector carboxilato.

en: How easily the electron cloud distorts. Governs the softer, less directional part of the bonding.
es: Con cuánta facilidad se deforma la nube electrónica. Gobierna la parte más blanda y menos direccional del enlace.

en: Recovered from the metal salt used, not from the element. This is what separates Fe(II) from Fe(III).
es: Recuperado de la sal metálica utilizada, no del elemento. Es lo que separa Fe(II) de Fe(III).

en: Ionic radius for that specific oxidation state and coordination number. Sets how many linkers fit around the metal.
es: Radio iónico para ese estado de oxidación y ese número de coordinación concretos. Fija cuántos conectores caben alrededor del metal.

en: Charge density: the field the metal projects onto its neighbours. Derived, and the most informative of the group.
es: Densidad de carga: el campo que el metal proyecta sobre sus vecinos. Derivada, y la más informativa del grupo.

en: ETL: extract, transform, load
es: ETL: extraer, transformar, cargar

en: Pull the data out of wherever it lives — a spreadsheet, an instrument file, a scanned report.
es: Saca los datos de donde sea que vivan: una hoja de cálculo, un fichero de instrumento, un informe escaneado.

en: Turn it into something consistent: same units, same names, same shape, with the errors found and fixed.
es: Conviértelos en algo coherente: mismas unidades, mismos nombres, misma forma, con los errores encontrados y corregidos.

en: Put it into the store the rest of the work reads from.
es: Déjalos en el almacén del que lee todo el resto del trabajo.

en: Two independent data streams arrive at this stage, and neither is usable as it stands. One is five years of manual synthesis records (mixtures, ratios, temperatures). The other is 1,877 raw diffractograms—thousands of noisy data points per sample that must be standardized into discrete numerical features.
es: A esta etapa llegan dos flujos de datos independientes, y ninguno es utilizable tal cual. Uno son cinco años de registros manuales de síntesis (mezclas, proporciones, temperaturas). El otro son 1.877 difractogramas en crudo: miles de puntos ruidosos por muestra que hay que estandarizar en características numéricas discretas.

en: The synthesis table needs cleaning and enrichment
es: La tabla de síntesis necesita limpieza y enriquecimiento

en: Normalising headers, turning free text into numbers, and replacing elements and linkers labels with their properties that explain its behavior.
es: Normalizar cabeceras, convertir texto libre en números, y sustituir las etiquetas de elementos y conectores por las propiedades que explican su comportamiento.

en: The diffractograms need signal processing
es: Los difractogramas necesitan procesado de señal

en: Separating the crystalline signal from the background, so that each curve collapses into a fixed set of comparable numbers.
es: Separar la señal cristalina del fondo, para que cada curva se reduzca a un conjunto fijo de números comparables.

en: Those are the **two sections of this screen**, and they are read one at a time — pick one below, and the buttons come back at the bottom to switch.
es: Esas son las **dos secciones de esta pantalla**, y se leen de una en una: elige una abajo, y los botones vuelven a aparecer al final para cambiar.

en: **Garbage in, garbage out**. This stage sets the quality for everything downstream.
es: **Basura entra, basura sale**. Esta etapa fija la calidad de todo lo que viene después.

en: Why this stage decides the ceiling
es: Por qué esta etapa decide el techo

en: A model is only as good as the feature matrix it trains on. Everything here exists to transform raw chemistry into rigorous, physically meaningful tabular numbers.
es: Un modelo no puede ser mejor que la matriz de características con la que entrena. Todo lo que hay aquí existe para convertir química en crudo en números tabulares rigurosos y con sentido físico.

en: Synthesis: Chemical plausibility over statistics
es: Síntesis: plausibilidad química por encima de la estadística

en: Cleaning spreadsheets required chemical insight, not just data profiling. Catching impossible units and hidden solvent fractions prevents corrupt numbers from entering training.
es: Limpiar las hojas de cálculo exigió criterio químico, no solo perfilado de datos. Cazar unidades imposibles y fracciones de disolvente ocultas impide que entren números corruptos al entrenamiento.

en: Characterization: Signal into structured features
es: Caracterización: de señal a características estructuradas

en: Diffraction patterns are compressed into discrete physical descriptors, preserving critical features like the amorphous halo without losing signal to baseline noise.
es: Los patrones de difracción se comprimen en descriptores físicos discretos, conservando rasgos críticos como el halo amorfo sin perder señal contra el ruido de la línea base.

en: The unified row: Recipes paired with outcomes
es: La fila unificada: recetas emparejadas con resultados

en: Recipes without outcomes cannot train a model; outcomes without recipes explain nothing. The true deliverable is the clean relational join: one complete experiment per row.
es: Recetas sin resultados no entrenan nada; resultados sin recetas no explican nada. El entregable de verdad es el JOIN relacional limpio: un experimento completo por fila.

en: Domain knowledge is irreplaceable during data preparation: only a chemist can distinguish an impossible data error from a genuine, unexpected scientific discovery.
es: El conocimiento del dominio es insustituible durante la preparación de datos: solo un químico distingue un error imposible de un hallazgo científico genuino e inesperado.

en: Identity & audit
es: Identidad y auditoría

en: Who ran it, when, under which unit, and in which well of the high-throughput plate. Not predictive, but it is what makes a row traceable to a physical notebook page — the ISO-17025 requirement that turns a spreadsheet into a record.
es: Quién la hizo, cuándo, bajo qué unidad y en qué pocillo de la placa de alto rendimiento. No es predictivo, pero es lo que hace una fila rastreable hasta una página física de cuaderno: el requisito ISO-17025 que convierte una hoja de cálculo en un registro.

en: The chemistry the experiment was meant to be. **lm_ratio** — linker to metal — is the single most argued-over number in the whole table: it decides whether there is enough organic strut to build a framework at all.
es: La química que el experimento pretendía ser. **lm_ratio** —conector frente a metal— es el número más discutido de toda la tabla: decide si hay suficiente puntal orgánico para levantar una red.

en: Six solvents recorded as absolute volumes in millilitres. Absolute volumes are not comparable between a 1,5 mL vial and a 15 mL autoclave, so they are later converted into **fractions of the total**, plus a `fill_fraction` that says how full the reactor was.
es: Seis disolventes registrados como volúmenes absolutos en mililitros. Los volúmenes absolutos no son comparables entre un vial de 1,5 mL y un autoclave de 15 mL, así que después se convierten en **fracciones del total**, más un `fill_fraction` que dice cuán lleno estaba el reactor.

en: Written in the notebooks as free text — *"ramp to 120 °C over 2 h, hold 48 h, cool overnight"*. Parsed into four numbers, because the **rate** of heating and cooling changes the product as much as the target temperature does.
es: Escritas en los cuadernos como texto libre: *"rampa a 120 °C en 2 h, mantener 48 h, enfriar toda la noche"*. Se parsean en cuatro números, porque la **velocidad** de calentamiento y de enfriamiento cambia el producto tanto como la temperatura objetivo.

en: Ten additives, each stored as **mmol of active species** rather than as microlitres of stock solution. The conversion is the single most delicate transformation in the notebook: a modulator added as an aqueous acid also contributes water, and forgetting that corrupts the solvent fractions above.
es: Diez aditivos, cada uno guardado como **mmol de especie activa** y no como microlitros de disolución madre. La conversión es la transformación más delicada del cuaderno: un modulador añadido como ácido acuoso también aporta agua, y olvidarlo corrompe las fracciones de disolvente de arriba.

en: One row per synthesis, 46 columns. These eight are the ones a chemist would recognise first.
es: Una fila por síntesis, 46 columnas. Estas ocho son las que un químico reconocería primero.

en: Synthetic rows. The values sit inside the real observed ranges but no row corresponds to an actual experiment; sample codes are placeholders and linker identities are withheld.
es: Filas sintéticas. Los valores están dentro de los rangos reales observados, pero ninguna fila corresponde a un experimento real; los códigos de muestra son marcadores y las identidades de los conectores se omiten.

en: In reticular chemistry, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) serves as the primary diagnostic benchmark. Fast and non-destructive, it provides immediate insight into long-range periodic order.
es: En química reticular, la difracción de rayos X de polvo (PXRD) es el diagnóstico de referencia. Rápida y no destructiva, da información inmediata sobre el orden periódico de largo alcance.

en: PXRD requires only milligrams and minutes of scan time without consuming the sample. It immediately reveals whether the reaction produced sharp Bragg reflections (characteristic of an ordered framework) or a diffuse amorphous profile, establishing whether the target crystalline phase assembled before investing in advanced characterization.
es: La PXRD solo necesita miligramos y minutos de barrido, sin consumir la muestra. Revela de inmediato si la reacción produjo reflexiones de Bragg afiladas (características de una red ordenada) o un perfil amorfo difuso, y así establece si la fase cristalina buscada se ensambló antes de invertir en caracterización avanzada.

en: For periodic MOFs, long-range order dictates pore architecture, internal surface area, and host-guest properties. Predicting whether a specific combination of synthetic variables will yield a crystalline network enables rational navigation of reaction space, filtering out unpromising synthesis conditions beforehand.
es: En los MOF periódicos, el orden de largo alcance dicta la arquitectura del poro, la superficie interna y las propiedades huésped-anfitrión. Predecir si una combinación concreta de variables de síntesis dará una red cristalina permite navegar el espacio de reacción de forma racional, descartando de antemano las condiciones poco prometedoras.

en: Is it crystalline?
es: ¿Es cristalino?

en: Minutes. Non-destructive. Run on everything.
es: Minutos. No destructiva. Se hace a todo.

en: FTIR · UV-Vis · ICP · EA
es: FTIR · UV-Vis · ICP · EA

en: Which groups, which gap, which composition?
es: ¿Qué grupos, qué band gap, qué composición?

en: Confirmatory. Only once the material is worth confirming.
es: Confirmatoria. Solo cuando el material merece confirmarse.

en: Up to what temperature does it survive?
es: ¿Hasta qué temperatura sobrevive?

en: Hours. Consumes the sample.
es: Horas. Consume la muestra.

en: What do the crystals look like?
es: ¿Qué aspecto tienen los cristales?

en: Booked instrument time, and a trained operator.
es: Tiempo de instrumento reservado, y un operador con formación.

en: Is it actually porous, and how much?
es: ¿Es poroso de verdad, y cuánto?

en: A day per sample. Needs prior activation.
es: Un día por muestra. Necesita activación previa.

en: Two folders, two clearances
es: Dos carpetas, dos niveles de acceso

en: Read every PDF in the corpus and stamp it with a sensitivity label before anything else happens to it.
es: Leer cada PDF del corpus y sellarlo con una etiqueta de sensibilidad antes de que le pase nada más.

en: `sensitivity` - PUBLIC or INTERNAL, decided by the folder the file was sitting in
es: `sensitivity` - PUBLIC o INTERNAL, según la carpeta en la que estuviera el fichero

en: `doc_type` - PAPER, SUPPORTING_INFORMATION or LAB_NOTEBOOK
es: `doc_type` - PAPER, SUPPORTING_INFORMATION o LAB_NOTEBOOK

en: `file_name` and `file_path`, so any passage can be traced back to its source
es: `file_name` y `file_path`, para poder rastrear cualquier pasaje hasta su fuente

en: The label comes from the folder, not from a field somebody fills in. A structural rule cannot be forgotten on a busy day - and this one decides what the assistant may repeat to a stranger.
es: La etiqueta viene de la carpeta, no de un campo que alguien rellena. Una regla estructural no se puede olvidar en un día ajetreado, y esta decide qué puede repetirle el asistente a un desconocido.

en: The MD5 gate
es: La barrera del MD5

en: Compare the checksum of every file against what is already indexed, and let through only what is new.
es: Comparar la suma de comprobación de cada fichero con lo que ya está indexado, y dejar pasar solo lo nuevo.

en: The binary MD5 of each file
es: El MD5 binario de cada fichero

en: A Merge in *keep non-matches* mode: what is already registered simply does not continue
es: Un Merge en modo *quedarse con lo que no casa*: lo ya registrado sencillamente no continúa

en: This is what makes the ingestion idempotent. Re-running it over the whole corpus costs a few seconds of hashing instead of re-embedding 87,765 passages - and, more importantly, it cannot silently double the corpus and fill retrieval with near-identical neighbours.
es: Esto es lo que hace idempotente la ingesta. Volver a lanzarla sobre el corpus entero cuesta unos segundos de hashing en vez de reembeber 87.765 pasajes y, más importante, no puede duplicar el corpus en silencio y llenar la recuperación de vecinos casi idénticos.

en: Split, embed, store
es: Trocear, embeber, guardar

en: Turn each document into passages a model can retrieve, and write them to pgvector beside their catalogue entry.
es: Convertir cada documento en pasajes que un modelo pueda recuperar, y escribirlos en pgvector junto a su entrada de catálogo.

en: Passages of **1,200 characters with 250 of overlap** - 87,765 of them
es: Pasajes de **1.200 caracteres con 250 de solape**: 87.765 en total

en: One 1,024-dimension vector each, from `bge-m3` running locally in Ollama
es: Un vector de 1.024 dimensiones cada uno, de `bge-m3` corriendo en local con Ollama

en: A row in `rag_documents` per source file, one in `rag_chunks` per passage
es: Una fila en `rag_documents` por fichero fuente, y una en `rag_chunks` por pasaje

en: The embeddings node is shared with the query side on purpose. If indexing and searching used different models, the store would return plausible nonsense and never raise an error. Sharing one node makes that mismatch structurally impossible.
es: El nodo de embeddings se comparte con el lado de la consulta a propósito. Si indexar y buscar usaran modelos distintos, el almacén devolvería tonterías verosímiles sin dar nunca un error. Compartir un solo nodo hace ese desajuste estructuralmente imposible.

en: Who is asking
es: Quién pregunta

en: Identify the caller and settle what they are allowed to see, before a single token reaches a language model.
es: Identificar a quien llama y resolver qué puede ver, antes de que un solo token llegue a un modelo de lenguaje.

en: A caller identity and session id, carried into every downstream tool call
es: Una identidad de quien llama y un id de sesión, que viajan a todas las llamadas de herramienta aguas abajo

en: A verdict against `authorized_researchers`
es: Un veredicto contra `authorized_researchers`

en: A logged, answered refusal for anyone who does not clear it
es: Un rechazo registrado y respondido para quien no lo supere

en: A denied request is written to the log and gets a reply. Silent failure is the enemy here: an assistant that simply stops looks identical to one that is broken.
es: Una petición denegada se escribe en el log y recibe respuesta. El fallo silencioso es el enemigo aquí: un asistente que simplemente se para es indistinguible de uno roto.

en: Gemini, with a local understudy
es: Gemini, con un suplente local

en: Answer the question using the tools, and keep answering when the cloud model is not there.
es: Responder a la pregunta usando las herramientas, y seguir respondiendo cuando el modelo en la nube no está.

en: A windowed conversation memory, shared by both agents
es: Una memoria de conversación por ventana, compartida por los dos agentes

en: A complete second Agent node wired to **Qwen3 14B** in local Ollama, hanging off the error output of the first
es: Un segundo nodo Agent completo conectado a **Qwen3 14B** en Ollama local, colgando de la salida de error del primero

en: A row in `agent_chat_log` for every exchange, written before the reply goes back
es: Una fila en `agent_chat_log` por cada intercambio, escrita antes de devolver la respuesta

en: The Agent node refuses two language models at once - "Only 1 ai_languageModel sub-nodes are/is allowed to be connected" - and the documented fallback switch does not exist in this installation. So the fallback is built at workflow level instead, and it was verified by forcing a real Gemini failure rather than by assuming.
es: El nodo Agent se niega a aceptar dos modelos de lenguaje a la vez ("Only 1 ai_languageModel sub-nodes are/is allowed to be connected") y el conmutador de fallback documentado no existe en esta instalación. Así que el fallback se construye a nivel de flujo, y se verificó forzando un fallo real de Gemini en vez de darlo por hecho.

en: Nine powers, one switched off
es: Nueve poderes, uno apagado

en: Give the assistant everything it needs to answer, and nothing it needs to invent.
es: Darle al asistente todo lo que necesita para responder, y nada que necesite inventarse.

en: Six tools that read the laboratory: syntheses, characterisation, one full sample, statistics, the bibliography and the schema dictionary
es: Seis herramientas que leen el laboratorio: síntesis, caracterización, una muestra completa, estadísticas, la bibliografía y el diccionario del esquema

en: One semantic search across the 87,765 passages
es: Una búsqueda semántica sobre los 87.765 pasajes

en: Two that walk the knowledge graph: resolve the node, then explore up to three hops
es: Dos que recorren el grafo de conocimiento: resolver el nodo, y luego explorar hasta tres saltos

en: Every one is a call to a stored SQL function with typed parameters - the assistant never writes SQL. What it can ask is bounded by the database rather than by how well the prompt is worded. The Cohere reranker is wired and deliberately disabled: it is the one component that would send passage text to a third party.
es: Cada una es una llamada a una función SQL almacenada con parámetros tipados: el asistente nunca escribe SQL. Lo que puede preguntar lo acota la base de datos y no lo bien redactado que esté el prompt. El reordenador de Cohere está conectado y desactivado a propósito: es el único componente que enviaría texto de los pasajes a un tercero.

en: Contextual retrieval, and an honest result
es: Recuperación contextual, y un resultado honesto

en: Chunking destroys context. Cut a paper into 1,200-character passages and a sentence like *"the yield rose to 68 % under these conditions"* loses which compound, which conditions, which paper. Retrieval then returns something locally relevant and globally meaningless.
es: Trocear destruye el contexto. Corta un artículo en pasajes de 1.200 caracteres y una frase como *"el rendimiento subió al 68 % en estas condiciones"* pierde de qué compuesto, qué condiciones y qué artículo habla. La recuperación devuelve entonces algo relevante en local y sin sentido en global.

en: The fix, published by **Anthropic as contextual retrieval**, is to have an LLM write one short sentence situating each passage inside its own document, prepend it, and embed *that*. It is built here end to end: `rag_chunk_context` holds **87,765 context sentences**, one per passage, and `rag_chunks.embedding_v2` holds the re-embedding of passage-plus-context.
es: La solución, publicada por **Anthropic como recuperación contextual**, es que un LLM escriba una frase corta que sitúe cada pasaje dentro de su propio documento, anteponerla y embeber *eso*. Está construida aquí de principio a fin: `rag_chunk_context` guarda **87.765 frases de contexto**, una por pasaje, y `rag_chunks.embedding_v2` guarda el reembebido de pasaje más contexto.

en: **The gain was modest.** Compared live against the original embeddings on real questions, similarities came out 0.005-0.01 higher and only one or two of every four retrieved passages changed. Nothing like the improvement the technique reports.
es: **La ganancia fue modesta.** Comparada en vivo contra los embeddings originales sobre preguntas reales, las similitudes salieron entre 0,005 y 0,01 más altas y solo cambiaron uno o dos de cada cuatro pasajes recuperados. Nada que ver con la mejora que reporta la técnica.

en: The explanation is the corpus, not the method. The published measurements come from material whose fragments lean heavily on their surroundings. A chemistry paper is written in paragraphs that already name their own compound and their own conditions, so there was less missing context to restore. **The technique is sound; this corpus had little room for it to help.**
es: La explicación es el corpus, no el método. Las medidas publicadas vienen de material cuyos fragmentos se apoyan mucho en lo que tienen alrededor. Un artículo de química está escrito en párrafos que ya nombran su propio compuesto y sus propias condiciones, así que había menos contexto que restaurar. **La técnica es buena; este corpus tenía poco margen para que ayudara.**

en: So `embedding_v2` is built, populated, and deliberately **not promoted** to the default search. Switching it on is one line. What is missing is the measurement that would justify it: the same comparison over enough questions to tell a real gain from noise.

en: Does any single variable separate the classes?
Which variables are being tested here

The **29 PXRD descriptors** extracted from each diffractogram: peak count, crystalline fraction, peak width, entropy, signal-to-noise and the rest. Not the synthesis conditions. The question is whether any single measurement taken *from the pattern* is enough, on its own, to tell the three classes apart.
What each class looks like as numbers
**No peaks at all** (`n_peaks` = 0). 88 % of the scattered area sits under the diffuse halo, and peak-to-background stays near **0.03**.
A handful of **broad** reflections: median 8 peaks at **0.240°** FWHM, with about half the area crystalline and peak-to-background near **1.19**.
Many **sharp** reflections: median 19 peaks at **0.162°** FWHM, **77 %** crystalline fraction, and peak-to-background at **9.42**.
Where those 29 numbers come from, descriptor by descriptor

They do order the classes cleanly: every descriptor tested rises or falls **monotonically** from amorphous through incipient to crystalline. The numbers agree with the human verdicts on the direction of the effect.

But ordering is not separating. In the box plots below the boxes **overlap for every variable tested**: an incipient sample and a crystalline one can share the same peak count, the same width, the same entropy. That overlap is the definition of a multivariate problem, and the reason a model is needed instead of a threshold.
The confounder that nearly ruined the analysis
The record holds three ways of making a material, and version 2 of this analysis mixed them without looking. The numbers:

**Zero amorphous samples in microwave.** Detecting that a synthesis was microwave-assisted, even indirectly through reactor volume or year, lets a model answer CRYSTALLINE and be right 96% of the time. Those 94 cases are 5% of the dataset and 27% of the crystalline class.
The cause is selection bias

Combinatorial screening is exploratory, so it is full of failures. Standard and microwave synthesis are used once the recipe is known to work. "Synthesis type" largely encodes **whether the outcome was already known**.
And the physics differ
Microwave heating is localised and fast, favouring kinetic phases over thermodynamic ones. Mixing the methods forces the model to learn two physics as one.
It is the only subset without success bias: it was designed to explore, not to confirm.
It is what we actually want to predict — the next plate is an HTS plate.
It is a single thermal regime, so the model learns one physics, not two.

The price is stated: 90 of the 330 crystalline cases are lost, 27%, and the minority class becomes scarcer still. The alternative is **a higher score that measures the synthesis method** instead of the chemistry.
Correlation: two different questions
Do two input variables move together?
This one is about **interpretation**, not about performance.
What to look for
Not zero correlation — knowing **where** it is not zero.
Why it matters

Two columns carrying nearly the same information make the model **split the credit between them arbitrarily**. Reading "this variable barely matters" would then be a mistake: it matters, but its twin took the credit.
What is done about it
The final interpretation is read **by chemical block**, never variable by variable.
A map with red blocks is not a problem. Here they are mostly properties of the same metal, correlated **by physics**: the electronegativity and hardness of a cation are not independent in nature.
Does each variable relate to the target?
This is the one you **do** want to be high — it is literally the signal the model will exploit.
Why Pearson does not apply
The target is **categorical with three levels**, not a number. A Pearson coefficient between "amorphous" and a temperature is undefined.
What is used instead
The correlation ratio **η²** for numeric against categorical, and **Cramér's V** for categorical against categorical.
How to read it
Both are plotted below, on the same scale, so a weak association looks weak.
The blank cells are not missing data

A white square means the correlation **is not defined**, not that a value was lost. `reactor_volume_ml` is 2.5 mL in every high-throughput synthesis, so its variance is zero and any correlation with it divides by zero.

It follows that `fill_fraction` is exactly `total_volume_ml / 2.5`: the same variable rescaled, across all 1,516 rows. **Both columns are excluded from the model** — zero variance for one, perfect collinearity for the other.

**Correlation is not causation**. These plots measure whether two things move together, nothing more. Temperature appearing associated with crystallinity does not demonstrate that raising it causes crystallisation: the two may share a common cause, or it may be a coincidence of this record. Establishing causation requires intervening, changing only the temperature and seeing what happens.
The process variables are **discrete in practice**
A continuous variable on paper is not continuous in the record. Over the training set, three of the main process variables take these values and no others:
And they are not evenly used either: **710 of the syntheses sit at 150 °C** and 370 at 120 °C, so two settings out of nine cover seven tenths of the record.
This reflects how combinatorial synthesis is designed: **fix a grid of conditions and sweep composition**. A chemist filling a 24-well plate picks round numbers.

It carries a consequence for interpretation: **a variable that was barely varied cannot explain much variance, however important it is chemically**. Reaction time takes three values in this record, so a model that finds it unimportant is describing the record, not the chemistry.
From the full record to the training set
The laboratory performed **2,167 syntheses**. The chain below counts **rows of the feature table**, which is why it starts at 2,152: those are the syntheses the pipeline could turn into features.

Each step removes exactly one filter from the query the model registry stores for this dataset, so the last line is the number the registry holds. **Every drop is a deliberate exclusion with a stated reason.**

By the last row the model is no longer a model of this laboratory’s chemistry: it is a model of **combinatorial syntheses that produced a powder someone was willing to judge**. Everything below refers to those 1,516 rows unless it says otherwise.
The target: how much imbalance there is
Across the 1,516 training rows the three classes are far from equally common, and that is chemistry rather than sampling: most attempts land somewhere in between.

A model that learns nothing at all, always answering **INCIPIENT**, is right 64% of the time. That is why every metric in this project is quoted against that floor rather than against zero: reporting "64% accuracy" would describe a model that does nothing.

The gap between the largest and smallest class is **6 : 1**, and it is sharper than over the whole record, because restricting to high-throughput synthesis removed material that was almost entirely crystalline. It is handled by **weighting the classes inside each model**, which is simpler than resampling and does not invent samples that were never made.
Exploratory Data Analysis
Plot every variable, count what is missing, check whether the classes are balanced and whether two columns say the same thing twice.
It produces no model and no metric, which is why it gets skipped. What it produces is decisions: which rows to drop, which columns cannot be trusted.
Separate signal that comes from the chemistry from signal that comes from how the data was collected.
**A model cannot warn you about a problem it has learned to exploit.** If a confounder sits in the training data, cross-validation rewards the model for using it. The only place to catch it is here.
One synthesis method had produced no amorphous samples at all — so the method itself predicted the answer
Five kinds of gap
Nine per cent missing, from five unrelated causes, each needing a different fix
A 6 : 1 imbalance
Between the largest and smallest class, enough to make accuracy meaningless
Rows that are not independent of one another, which makes a random split lie
Hidden structure: why a random split would lie

Each row is **one synthesis**: one well of a 24-well plate, with its conditions and the verdict on its diffractogram. Those rows are **not independent of one another**. A plate is a batch prepared on the same day, with the same linker, the same thermal ramp and often the same metal, sweeping one variable. And plates are internally homogeneous: knowing one well tells you most of what its 23 neighbours did.

A random split would put samples from the same plate in both training and test. The model would not need to learn any chemistry: **recognising the plate would be enough**. The score would come out inflated and false. Validation therefore groups by plate, so no plate ever appears on both sides.

This compounds with the class imbalance. With **64% of samples incipient** and whole plates almost uniformly one class, a lucky split can hand the test set a plate that is 90% incipient, where the do-nothing baseline scores 90% and any model looks brilliant. Grouping by plate stops the split from choosing its own difficulty.

There is temporal drift too: the class proportions change year on year, because the laboratory was learning. Every bar carries its count, because **a proportion without its sample size misleads**: a year with seven samples shows a 100% bar that means nothing.
A single "9% missing" figure hides unrelated problems, and only some of them are what imputation assumes.
Where the modulator descriptors come from

Ten columns of acids, nearly all zero in any given row, would let the model memorise which plate used which reagent instead of learning chemistry. So they were **grouped by chemical role** (carboxylic, strong acid, HF, base, fluorinated) and summed. Two extra columns carry the **mean pKa and mean logP of the acids present**, weighted by how much of each was added, so the chemistry the sum discards is not lost.
**"Carboxylic" here means weak carboxylic.** Trifluoroacetic acid is grouped with the strong acids: the criterion was pKa, not functional family, and at pKa 0.23 it behaves like one. 82 syntheses.
**The pKa and logP values carry no citation.** They are standard aqueous figures at 25 °C written into the SQL. Every other chemical property in the model traces to a reference in `property_sources`.
The PCA projection
This is a diagnostic, not a model.
What a PCA does
Each synthesis is a point in a space with one dimension per variable, which cannot be looked at directly.
PCA finds the **direction along which the points are most spread out**, then the most spread-out direction perpendicular to it, and so on.
Projecting onto the first two gives a flat picture that keeps as much of the original spread as any flat picture can.
It is a **change of viewpoint, not a summary**: nothing is discarded.
What goes in

The **38 synthesis-condition columns**: metal properties, linker properties, solvent fractions, thermal ramp and modulators. Not the 29 PXRD descriptors, which describe the outcome. The question is whether what was *done* already separates the outcomes.
How it is built
**Standardise** the numeric variables after imputation. Without it, reaction time (up to 96) would crush a solvent fraction (0 to 1) through the scale of its units alone.
**Find the direction of maximum variance**, a linear combination of every variable, and call it the first component. Then the maximum remaining variance perpendicular to it, and so on.
**Project** the samples onto those components so they can be drawn.
PCA uses every variable and **does not know the classes**: it is unsupervised, and the colours are painted on afterwards. So any separation that appears is real structure in the synthesis conditions.
There is structure, but the classes overlap heavily. The problem is genuinely multivariate and genuinely hard.
Adding a third component reveals no hidden separation. That is a useful negative result: there is **no plane that separates the classes**, which already predicts that no linear model will shine.

Reaching 90% of the variance takes many components. The information is spread across many variables rather than concentrated in two or three — so reducing dimensionality before modeling would throw away signal, and PCA is not used in the final pipeline.
Neat liquid modulators stored as µmol but labelled mmol — a factor of 1,000
The median formic acid value read 1,168 "mmol", which is 54 g of formic acid in a 2.5 mL reactor. Physically impossible.
Formula corrected in notebook 01; stored values divided by 1,000.
Adding mmol to µmol erased HCl from the strong-acid feature
A consequence of defect 1: HCl contributed ~0.004 against TFA at ~600.
With coherent units, the most-used modulator in the whole dataset — 393 syntheses — becomes visible to the model again.
Synthesis type absent as a variable, while being the largest confounder
Microwave runs are 95.7% crystalline against 11.0% for combinatorial screening.
Restrict training to high-throughput synthesis only.
1-propanol and DEF missing from the feature view
Solvent fractions summed to 0.789 instead of 1.
All six solvents included.
The liquid modulator is sometimes the solvent, and was not counted as medium
After fixing defect 4 the volume still did not close. One synthesis used 1.35 mL of propionic acid out of 1.5 mL total.
A modulator fraction reconstructed from the millimoles.
HF grouped with HCl despite a different chemical role
Chemical argument: HF is a mineralising agent, and some frameworks only crystallise in its presence.
Its own column, 25 syntheses.
22 rows lost their ionic radius to a non-breaking space
A U+00A0 character inside precursor strings such as "MgCl2 · 6H2O" stopped them matching the lookup table.
The join was normalised, rather than adding typographic variants by hand — that is a race you do not win.
Exclusion as a label, never as a deletion

Auditing the dataset uncovered 113 problematic entries: 43 duplicate scans (re-runs, washed samples) that would bias training, and 70 amorphous runs contaminated with metal oxide peaks that would poison class labels

Instead of destructive hard-deletions, every case was flagged with ml_include = NO. In scientific databases, deleting destroys experimental history; explicit flagging preserves the audit trail while delivering clean data to the models.
In a scientific data store, **deleting destroys evidence and labelling preserves it**.
Imputation: tested, not assumed
Numeric gaps are filled with the median and categorical ones with the mode — always inside the cross-validation pipeline, never before it.

Imputing with the median of the whole dataset before splitting leaks information from the test fold into training: the test rows would have helped compute the median used on them. It is a subtle leak that inflates the result while nothing appears to fail. Inside the pipeline, each fold computes its median from its own data only.

Flagging which values were missing adds nothing, so the simple version stays. That is worth recording precisely because it is a negative result: knowing that missingness is not informative means the gaps are recording accidents, not a pattern with chemical meaning.
Modulators reach the reactor in two physically different forms, and each needs its own arithmetic.
Type A — aqueous molar solutions
HCl, HF and KOH are dosed as solutions of known molarity, so the active amount follows directly from volume times concentration.
Type B — neat organic liquids
Formic, acetic, propionic, trifluoroacetic, triflic and methanesulfonic acids, plus triethylamine, are pipetted pure. The amount has to be reconstructed from density, purity and molecular weight.
Tannic acid: a chemical decision, then confirmed by measurement

24 samples used tannic acid, a polyphenol and the only non-phosphonate chemistry in the record. Its denticity is not well defined — with roughly 25 phenolic hydroxyls there is no meaningful number of binding "teeth". The argument for removing them is chemical and comes first: 24 samples are not enough for a model to learn a separate chemical family, and their presence forces the linker descriptors to describe two incompatible things at once.
Removing them raises macro F1 from 0.495 to 0.527, and MCC from 0.266 to 0.312.

Choosing what to remove because it improves the metric is a way of cheating: the number can always be raised by dropping the hard cases. Here the order was the right one — **chemical argument first, verification second** — and that is what makes the exclusion legitimate. Had the criterion been "let us try removing things and see what goes up", the result would be worth nothing.
Parsing thermal ramps written in prose
The spreadsheet recorded thermal programs as free text. They are parsed into initial, target and final temperature, plateau hours, and two slopes in °C per minute.
The correction that mattered more than the seven
Wherever the solvent breakdown failed to account for the total volume — about 18% of rows — the fractions were being stored as 0. They are now NULL, with an explicit completeness flag.

Writing a 0 where the value is unknown is not neutral: it asserts something false. "This synthesis contained no methanol" and "how much methanol it contained was never recorded" are different statements, and a model given a 0 has no way to tell them apart.
An honest reading of the performance
The full model roughly doubles the trivial baseline and reaches a Matthews correlation of 0.31, a real but moderate association. Two features of the result matter more than that headline.
Three quarters of the crystalline syntheses are not recovered

Recall on the crystalline class is **0.25** under the grouped cross-validation. That is the figure to quote: the tool exists to shortlist promising conditions, so it governs practical value far more than the aggregate does.
The confusion matrix above reads **0.53** for the same class — because it is one held-out split, not the five-fold average. A lucky set of plates flatters the smallest class.
Cause: **167 crystalline examples against 967 incipient**, and the crystalline class is the most heterogeneous. There are many ways for a framework to crystallise and only one way for it not to.
The actionable model sits close to the limit of the data
Stripped of metal and linker chemistry, macro F1 falls to **0.393** and MCC to **0.095**.
Above chance — and not yet a basis for recommending conditions.
This is the question the laboratory actually asks, so it is the more important of the two results.
The limit lies in the experimental record, not in the model

Across five years the record contains 15 distinct target temperatures and 11 reaction times, and the subset the model was trained on is poorer still — **9 temperatures and 3 reaction times**. They were also varied in a manner confounded with chemistry: each campaign swept one factor within one metal-linker system. A supervised model cannot estimate the effect of a variable that was held nearly constant, nor separate an effect from a factor it always co-occurred with. This is a property of the data, and no choice of algorithm or hyperparameter can recover information the experiments did not generate.

Hyperparameter optimisation on this dataset can reasonably be expected to yield an improvement of 0.02 to 0.05 in macro F1. It is worth doing for methodological completeness; it is not a route to a materially better model.
What would improve it, in order of expected return

Vary temperature, time and modulator finely **within a single metal-linker system**. It attacks the confounding head-on and costs one or two plates — by a wide margin the most efficient intervention available.
With **167** in the training set, the minority class is the binding constraint on every metric above. Nothing algorithmic gets around it.
**18 %** of rows lack the breakdown, and that block currently scores as noise. Its real contribution cannot even be measured until the medium is written down completely.
A continuous crystallinity index may carry more than a three-way class — though the three classes remain the judgement the bench actually recorded.

The score is defensible: cross-validated with plates as groups, computed after seven data defects were corrected, and reported alongside the baseline that gives it meaning. The limitation is one of experimental design rather than of the model, which makes it a specific and actionable experiment.
The chemical reading, by block rather than variable by variable

With strongly correlated variables, any importance method splits the credit arbitrarily. Interpreting Pauling electronegativity in isolation from absolute hardness would be over-reading. The block-level split is the defensible reading.
Dominant, by a wide margin

It enters through ionic radius and charge-over-radius, which together give the **charge density** of the cation. That charge density governs the strength of the metal-phosphonate interaction, and with it whether the system has time to order or precipitates amorphous.
Second, ahead of linker chemistry

This qualifies the easy reading of the headline numbers. Conditions do contribute, but only in combination with the chemistry: the actionable model, which uses them alone, stalls at 0.41. Temperature and time help decide within a metal-linker system, not between systems. Both statements are true and have to be read together.
Negative importance overall

Not a calculation error: shuffling those variables slightly improves the model, which is the operational definition of noise. It has an identifiable cause — the 18% of rows with no solvent breakdown — and a practical consequence: they are candidates for removal next time round, and their real value will not be known until the medium is recorded completely.

Permutation importance tends to split and to understate when variables are correlated: if two columns say almost the same thing, shuffling one barely hurts the model because the other covers the gap. So the absolute values should not be read as "percentage of the chemistry explained", and the block-level split is more reliable than any individual variable.

"It does not matter" and "it was not explored" are different claims, and only the second is actionable. The model is not saying temperature is irrelevant to phosphonate crystallisation; it is saying that in this record it **was not varied enough to be learnable**. The instruction that follows is experimental: vary it.
Where it goes wrong, and whether the errors make chemical sense
A confusion matrix shows the direction of the errors, not just how many there are. Here the ordinal pattern holds clearly one way and only half-way the other.

For amorphous samples the behaviour is what you would hope: when it fails, it confuses "nothing" with "almost nothing", which in the diffractogram itself is a matter of degree and something two experts could disagree about. The severe error — calling an amorphous sample crystalline — is rare.

For crystalline samples it is not. Roughly one in six is classified as amorphous, the most serious error available. The model does not recognise the minority class well, and when it loses it, it loses it completely. With 167 cases against 967 incipient, and the most heterogeneous class of the three (many ways to crystallise, one way not to), this was predictable. It remains the model's main weakness.

For the intended use, ranking candidates and filling the next plate, what matters is that good candidates rise in the ranking rather than that the label is exact. But the model makes a serious mistake on **22% of crystalline samples**, and that figure has to be quoted alongside the aggregate.
There is real predictive signal, and it is modest
The best full model reaches a macro F1 of about 0.52 against 0.26 for the baseline, twice as good. MCC lands near 0.31: a real association, but far from strong.
Excluding the confounded syntheses costs 0.10 of macro F1

Removing microwave and standard solvothermal runs drops the score from 0.62 to 0.52. That gap **measures the portion of the score that came from identifying the synthesis method** rather than the chemistry.
The actionable model drops further, and that answers the objection

Without metal and linker chemistry the best model falls to 0.393 with MCC near 0.095: above chance, but weak. Most of what the model distinguishes in this record is which metal-linker system was used, not which conditions were applied.
That does not make conditions chemically unimportant. In this record they were not varied enough to be learnable: **9 temperatures and 3 reaction times** across the training set.
Tree-based models win

Random Forest and LightGBM come out ahead of k-nearest neighbours and SVM. Methods that build boundaries from thresholds benefit from variables that mean what they say, which is what the unit corrections in the previous stage delivered.
Naive Bayes sinks below the baseline
It assumes the variables are independent given the class, and the correlation map shows strong blocks. Its failure measures how much that correlation matters, which is why it is on the list.

Ten models are compared, not one. Different model families assume different things about the shape of the boundary between classes, and with a new problem there is no way to know in advance which assumption is right.
Nothing: always the most frequent class
The bar. Everything else must clear it

It looks at no variable at all. It counts which class is commonest in the training data and answers that, every time. On this data it says INCIPIENT to everything and is right 64 % of the time. That is why accuracy is a useless headline here, and why this model is on the list: to give every other number a floor.
A linear boundary
Interpretable reference; if it suffices, it wins

Draws a straight dividing surface through the 39-dimensional space and reads each variable’s weight as its pull towards one class or another. If a straight line were enough, this would be the answer to keep: you can read the coefficients and argue about the chemistry. It is here to find out whether the problem needs anything more complicated.
Similar samples share an outcome
Purely local, with no global model

Builds no model. For a new synthesis it finds the fifteen most similar ones already on record and takes a vote. That makes it a direct test of a chemical intuition — that similar conditions give similar products — and it is unforgiving about badly scaled variables, which is part of what made it useful for spotting the unit defects.
Variables independent given the class
Its failure measures how much the correlation structure matters

Assumes every variable contributes independently, which in this data is plainly false: the electronegativity and the hardness of a cation are tied together by physics. It is on the list precisely so that assumption can fail visibly. It scores below the trivial baseline, and that gap is a measurement of how much the correlation structure matters.
A smooth non-linear boundary
Strong in medium dimension with few samples

Bends the boundary instead of keeping it straight, and cares only about the samples nearest the frontier. That makes it strong when there are many variables and few rows, which is this problem exactly. The price is that its decisions cannot be read off as "this variable mattered".
Threshold cuts, one at a time
Interpretable; the basis of what follows

Asks a chain of yes/no questions about single thresholds — is the temperature above 130, is there carboxylic modulator — until it reaches a verdict. Alone it overfits badly, but it is the building block of the four models below it, and it is the only one whose reasoning you can read out loud.
Many decorrelated trees
Robust, insensitive to hyperparameters

Grows hundreds of trees, each on a random slice of the rows and the columns, and averages them. The randomness is the point: individual trees overfit in different directions and the errors cancel. It is the model actually deployed here, chosen for being the best performer that is also hard to break by tuning it wrong.
Sequential trees correcting each other
Handles missing values natively

Instead of averaging independent trees, each new tree is fitted to the errors the previous ones left behind. It bins the variables first, which makes it fast, and it takes missing values without imputing them — relevant here, where a null pKa means "no carboxylic acid" rather than "unknown".
The industry reference

The same idea as above with a different growth strategy: it extends whichever leaf reduces the error most, rather than growing level by level. Fast and usually at the top of tabular benchmarks, which is why it is the yardstick. It is the model serving the actionable half of this project.
Boosting with regularisation

Boosting again, with an explicit penalty on tree complexity written into what it optimises. That extra brake is what usually separates it from LightGBM on small datasets, and with 1,516 rows this one qualifies as small.
Mean relative error, RMSE and R² do not apply here. They belong to regression and measure distance to a number. In classification you either get the class right or you do not.
Reading the SHAP plot

Each point is one synthesis. Its horizontal position is how far that variable pushed the prediction towards crystalline (right) or against it (left). The colour is the value of the variable — red high, blue low. So "red on the right" means high values of this variable favour crystallisation.
It complements permutation importance: that says how much a variable matters, this says in which direction and for which samples.
Two models, not one
The linker does not make a metal crystallise; it determines which material can exist at all. Changing it changes the chemistry, not a reaction condition.

So the variables split in two: **design variables** (metal and linker chemistry), which change the research target itself, and **process variables** (concentration, ligand-to-metal ratio, temperature, time, ramps, modulators, solvents), which can be changed within the same chemistry. One model is trained on each split.
Is there predictive signal in this record at all?
Best score of the two: **0.52 macro F1**, twice the baseline.
Most of that signal is the metal-linker system, so it cannot tell you what to change.
Given this chemistry, which conditions make it crystallise?
The question the bench actually asks, and the one that designs the next plate.
Falls to **0.393 macro F1**, MCC 0.095: above chance, not yet a basis for recommending conditions.
The gap between the two scores measures how much of the signal comes from the chemistry rather than from the conditions.
Validation grouped by plate
**A plate is 24 wells**: one block, one oven, one thermal programme, 24 compositions swept in parallel.
The training set is **1,516 syntheses across 68 plates**.
So a plate is a batch that shared a reactor, a day, a solvent bottle and an operator, not an administrative label.
**Stratified group k-fold, five folds.** Every plate stays entirely inside one fold, so no plate is ever in training and test at once.
**Without it**, a model can score well by recognising which plate a sample came from instead of learning any chemistry.
**The stratification** keeps class proportions even, so no fold ends up with almost no crystalline samples.
It costs performance. A random split would report a higher number for a model that had learned less.
